lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass. eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varies source locality) with Germany and France (where it varies language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: MillerKnoll has submitted refund claims on 'substantially all IEEPA tariffs paid' and had recognised nothing as of the FY26 10-K (20 July 2026), while CBP's CAPE refund channel has been paying out on a 60-90 day cycle since 20 April 2026 and a direct import peer, RH, recognised $55.1m of IEEPA refunds in the quarter ended 1 August 2026 - four weeks BEFORE MillerKnoll's quarter closed on 29 August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MillerKnoll has no prior refund print. The nearest analogue is a below-operating-income item: the $92.3m of goodwill impairments taken in Q3 FY25 (2026-03-26 print, +10.69%), where the market looked straight through the non-operating charge. That says items below the line neither help nor hurt this name much on their own, which is why this is sized at a fraction of the dollars rather than at them. findings.finding: The only demand evidence dated after MillerKnoll last guided (2026-06-24) is positive and comes from the largest direct competitor's primary release: HNI's 30 July 2026 Q2 exhibit states Workplace Furnishings orders +5% organic, that 'over the most recent five-week period, the year-over-year segment order growth rate accelerated', and guides segment volume growth positive in Q3 with high-single-digit organic growth in H2 - a period that sits inside MillerKnoll's fiscal Q1 (1 June - 29 August 2026), against a Q1 FY26 comparison of consolidated orders -5.4% and North America Contract orders -8.2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders alone have NOT paid on this name and I have sized for that: on 2026-03-25 North America Contract orders printed +13.1% reported and the stock fell 22.37% on a $0.02 EPS miss; on 2026-06-24 orders printed -6.3% with backlog -10.8% and the stock rose 12.01% on an EPS beat at the top of guidance. So the order line is only worth anything here through the FY27 guide ($3.93-4.13bn, ~5% growth), which is why I file this under guidance rather than reported_quarter: what an accelerating industry order rate buys is that the guide survives contact with an entering backlog down 10.8%.

findings.finding: The FY26 10-K discloses that the Global Retail reporting unit's fair value exceeded carrying value by just 1.1%, International Contract by 3.1%, and the Muuto and Knoll indefinite-lived trade names by 2.1% and 6.8% - cushions thin enough that the company says 'relatively modest adverse changes' in projected revenue growth or margin would produce material impairment charges, and MillerKnoll has form for taking interim impairments mid-year when performance disappoints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The direct precedent is MillerKnoll's own: in Q3 FY25 management identified interim triggering events and took $30.1m (Global Retail) and $62.2m (Holly Hunt) of non-cash goodwill impairment - and the stock rose 10.69% on that print (baseline, 2026-03-26... corrected: 2025-03-26, +10.69%). That history is the whole reason this is sized at -0.4 and not at -2: the charge itself is not what this stock pays for, and it only matters as a signal that management has cut the Global Retail plan, which would show up in the guide.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe is where this stock's last two large negative reactions originated: 2025-12-03 -9.48% and 2026-03-03 -5.56%, both quarters in which the FY26 EPS guide was under pressure. But the line has also gone the other way: on 2026-06-03 Thor cut the FY26 EPS guide from $3.75-4.25 to $3.30-3.80 and the stock rose 2.86%, and on 2025-09-24 it set an initial FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline and rose 6.10%. This is why the size is -2.0 and not larger.

findings.finding: Consensus Q4 revenue of $2.17-2.20bn requires Thor to print at or above the very top of its own unchanged FY26 guide: nine-month net sales are $7.297bn against a $9.0-9.5bn full-year range, so consensus sits at the 94th percentile of the guide while consensus EPS of $0.91-0.97 sits mid-range against the $0.71-1.21 the same guide implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Thor's reported-quarter surprises have not been what this stock trades on: on 2026-06-03 the quarter itself was weak (North American Towable net sales -24.6%, gross margin -470bp) and the stock still rose 2.86%. The two large down days, 2025-12-03 (-9.48%) and 2026-03-03 (-5.56%), both came with guidance pressure rather than with the printed quarter alone. That is the whole reason this finding is sized -1.0 against a -3.5% fundamental read.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-10, twelve days before this print, Thor abandoned the decentralised operating model it has run for decades and put all North American RV operations under a single president and a single CFO, with the stated objective of 'drive out costs within the Company to strengthen our earnings profile' and benefits on an 'accelerated timeline' relative to the two-group structure announced earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has paid for a self-help framing at a Q4 print before: on 2025-09-24, the equivalent event a year ago, Thor set an FY26 guide implying a 13-23% EPS decline off FY25's $4.85 and the stock rose 6.10%. The 2026-06-03 print, where management first put margin and cost language around a cut guide, went +2.86%. Both of the events on this line that carried a cost/structure narrative were bought.

findings.finding: Camping World, Thor's largest customer and holder of record US new-unit share above 29%, exited its June 2026 quarter with new vehicles on the lot down ~17% year on year in units (dollars down only ~5%), prior-model-year exposure on new RVs near 1% against over 6% a year earlier, and units aged more than 365 days cut by over 60%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Thor's FY26 has been a story of the towable guide being cut on 'cautious independent dealer ordering patterns' (2026-06-03 release); the 2025-09-24 Q4 print noted the opposite - 'initiatives to gain market share began to deliver results' with towable wholesale -10.1% - and the stock rose 6.10%. A dealer-restock framing at a Q4 print has been bought on this name.

outside_window.finding: FINRA's short-interest settlement for 2026-09-15 publishes on 2026-09-24, two sessions after the exit. Equibles models 5,091,730 shares short, +2.1% on the 2026-08-31 figure of 4,986,425 - shorts still building into the print - but the confirmation the market can trade on arrives after the window closes.

RVIA's August 2026 wholesale shipment report is not yet published as of 2026-09-21 - the RVIA reports page still shows July 2026 (19,948 units, 183,592 YTD) as the latest. It is the first read on Thor's FQ1 FY27 and on whether July's -25.6% motorhome print was an outlier, and it will land after this trade is closed.

The all-stock Patrick Industries / LCI Industries merger, targeting $150m of net annual run-rate cost savings, is expected to close in H1 2027. It consolidates two of Thor's three largest component suppliers into one counterparty and is a structural input cost question for FY27-28, not for this print.

lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest) cut the German/KBA European finding from -2.5 to -2.0: Europe is ~38% of revenue, the other 62% is North America where my read is mildly positive, and within Europe Thor is gaining share (24.4%), backlog is +1.0% and the euro is ~3-4% stronger year on year, so the reported European quarter can still print up in dollars. I also moved it firmly to lands_on=guidance rather than reported_quarter for the same reason.

Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broader series; macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until a company or direct counterparty says it) forced me to add the definitional caveat that KBA 'Wohnmobile' is narrower than CIVD 'Reisemobile', and to attach a direct competitor statement (Knaus Tabbert H1 2026: revenue -11.9%, 'cautious ordering behaviour from dealers') rather than let the government series stand alone. It did not kill the finding because the KBA months extend the CIVD series rather than contradicting it.

Lesson 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number, and resolve contradictions yourself) is what changed the revenue finding most: my RVIA bottom-up cross-check lands at ~$2.15bn, essentially at consensus, while backlog conversion lands at ~$1.96bn. Rather than leave a finding whose own text argues against it, I wrote the resolution into why_not_priced ($1.96-2.15bn bracket, ~$2.09bn point estimate) and cut the size from -1.5 to -1.0.

Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat) cut both negatives and stopped me filing positioning as a fifth, positive finding. Crowded short plus paid-for downside is a reason to shrink a negative, not a separate long; it belongs in positioning_check and in the gap between the finding sum and expected_move_pct, where it now is.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar, keep findings inside the window) got me two agreeing estimate sources plus the company's own guide, so no small-size cap applies; it also moved the FINRA 2026-09-24 settlement, the August RVIA report and the PATK/LCII close out of findings and into outside_window at zero.

Lesson 2 / 'least priced is not most likely right' cut the operating-model finding from +2.0 to +1.5, because what the 2026-09-10 document establishes is the reorganisation, not a quantified saving - the FY27 savings number is my inference and the finding text now says so.
The 'asking what the market missed generates pessimism' note is why I kept both positives rather than dropping them for being less dramatic; it did not change a size.

Net effect on the sums: pre_lessons impact_sum -0.5, emitted impact_sum -0.5 - equal by coincidence, because the file cut my negatives by 1.0 point and my positives by 1.0 point. Four individual sizes all moved; expected_move_pct came down from +1.5 to +1.0 on lesson 1 and lesson 7 (the reaction function's veto and the crowded short both argue for a smaller absolute reaction than my fundamental read).

findings.finding: Management has beaten the midpoint of its own quarterly revenue guide by +14.4% and +13.6% in the two immediately preceding quarters (Q2 guided RMB150-160m on 2025-12-02, printed RMB177.3m; Q3 guided RMB140-150m on 2026-03-12, printed RMB164.7m), and the Q4 guide of RMB130-140m was set on 2026-06-05 with two of the quarter's three months already elapsed -- so Q4 revenue should land near RMB148-155m and FY2026 revenue above the top of the revised RMB600-610m range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This exact line has been sold twice in a row: the Q2 print beat its guided range by 14.4% and the stock fell 16.26% (2026-03-12); the Q3 print beat its guided range by 13.6%, the CFO's own quote said results 'exceeded expectations on both revenue and gross margin', and the stock fell 24.89% (2026-06-05, close 2.37 -> 1.78 on 431,500 shares). A revenue beat against this company's own guide has a 0-for-2 record of paying, which is why this is sized at +0.5 and not at the beat.

findings.finding: The baseline's reaction history is wrong and the real one is far worse and far larger: rebuilt from confirmed release dates, this stock has fallen on 4 of 4 earnings prints -- 2025-09-17 (FY25 annual, bmo) -2.07%, 2025-12-02 -3.78%, 2026-03-12 -16.26%, 2026-06-05 -24.89% -- and the accessible wire copy misreports the 2026-06-05 move as -5.68% when the daily bars show 2.37 -> 1.78.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This finding IS the reaction history. The baseline carries median_abs_move_pct 3.78 and expected_move_pct 3.78 off three 6-K text matches on an inferred 61-day cadence it calls implausible; the sweep flagged baseline_history_trustworthy: false. findings.finding: The equity is a cash box with a live buyback the size of a fifth of itself: net cash US$91.76m against a US$100.07m market cap (EV US$8.31m), a new US$20.0m repurchase authorisation running 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30 that was announced with the guidance cut, US$12.8m already spent of the prior US$20m programme, and a board with form for autumn capital return (US$11m special dividend declared 2024-10-01). findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026 buyback was announced on 2026-06-05 inside the guidance-cut release and the stock still fell 24.89%, so an authorisation alone has demonstrably bought nothing here. What has never been tested at this price is a disclosed repurchase figure or a distribution: the only cash distribution in the company's history (2024-10-01, US$0.067/ordinary, US$0.201/ADS, ~US$11m) came two weeks after an annual results release, not inside one.

findings.finding: Two forward items surfaced in Chinese-language media in the ten days before the print and appear in no English coverage: the fifth-generation WAKUKU line '怪上头' went on sale offline on 2026-09-21 with the online drop at 20:00 Beijing on 2026-09-22 (the day of the call), and at CIFTIS on 2026-09-11 the company said overseas is ~20% of group annual revenue, products sell into 27 countries, and its target is overseas sales of 3-5x the prior year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Untested on this line at this name: the initial FY guide given at the last annual print (FY26 RMB750-800m, 2025-09-17) produced only -2.07%, the smallest reaction of the four, and it was then cut 22% eight months later -- so this shareholder base did not pay for an optimistic initial guide and was later proved right not to. Tomorrow's release should carry an initial FY2027 guide on the same template, and that, not the Q4 number, is the line that will set the move.
